{"result":"## Authorization and capture
Payments authorizes when the order moves to pending and captures later, from the
capture worker, CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES after authorization. The delay exists so that
an order edited within a few minutes of checkout can be re-authorized without a
refund. The provider holds an authorization for AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES; a hold that
lapses before the worker captures produces E4021 on capture. Capture is idempotent
by order id, so a second capture of the same order returns E5011 and is treated as
success. Captures that fail with a retryable provider error are retried up to
MAX_CAPTURE_RETRIES times with exponential backoff.

## Order lifecycle
An order starts as a quote. Adding a payment authorization moves it to pending.
Capture moves it to paid. Only paid orders appear in revenue reports, which is why
the paid-total report filters on status rather than on the presence of a payment row.
A cancelled order keeps its rows; cancellation releases any inventory reservation
and voids an uncaptured authorization.

## Service map
The platform is eight services behind one gateway. The gateway terminates TLS,
applies rate limits, and forwards to users, auth, orders, payments,
notifications, reporting, and search. Services call each other over internal
HTTP with the caller's session token forwarded only to the users and auth
services; every other internal call uses the calling service's own credential.
Orders calls payments to authorize and capture, payments calls notifications
when a capture succeeds or fails, and reporting reads a replica of the orders
and payments databases rather than calling either service."}

## Authorization and capture
Payments authorizes when the order moves to pending and captures later, from the
capture worker, CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES after authorization. The delay exists so that
an order edited within a few minutes of checkout can be re-authorized without a
refund. The provider holds an authorization for AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES; a hold that
lapses before the worker captures produces E4021 on capture. Capture is idempotent
by order id, so a second capture of the same order returns E5011 and is treated as
success. Captures that fail with a retryable provider error are retried up to
MAX_CAPTURE_RETRIES times with exponential backoff.

## Order lifecycle
An order starts as a quote. Adding a payment authorization moves it to pending.
Capture moves it to paid. Only paid orders appear in revenue reports, which is why
the paid-total report filters on status rather than on the presence of a payment row.
A cancelled order keeps its rows; cancellation releases any inventory reservation
and voids an uncaptured authorization.

## Service map
The platform is eight services behind one gateway. The gateway terminates TLS,
applies rate limits, and forwards to users, auth, orders, payments,
notifications, reporting, and search. Services call each other over internal
HTTP with the caller's session token forwarded only to the users and auth
services; every other internal call uses the calling service's own credential.
Orders calls payments to authorize and capture, payments calls notifications
when a capture succeeds or fails, and reporting reads a replica of the orders
and payments databases rather than calling either service.

content.text:
I couldn't find any fraud scoring thresholds in this project, so I don't have numbers to give you. I'm not going to guess at them.

Where I looked:

- **The code and config:** I searched for "fraud", "risk", "score", "threshold", "review" and "manual review" across all source, tests, scripts and config. None of them appear. The only "hold" match is `AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES` in `config/*/payments.env`, which is a different thing (see below).
- **Architecture docs (project-knowledge MCP):** there's no section on fraud or risk. The docs cover only: Service map, Order lifecycle, Authorization and capture, Soft deletes, Repository pattern, Notifications retry policy, Session handling, Reporting replica, Search indexing, and Configuration and secrets.
- **Payments config schema:** there are no fraud or review keys. The schema has only the API key, base URL, region, capture timeout and delay, auth hold, webhook secret and capture retries.
- **Service map:** it lists eight services (gateway, users, auth, orders, payments, notifications, reporting, search). None of them is a fraud or risk service.

**About `AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES`:** it isn't a manual-review hold. It sets how long the payment provider keeps a card authorization before it lapses. It's 60 in production and 10 in staging. It's unrelated to fraud scoring, but note that staging's 10 is below the default `CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES` of 15. If staging doesn't override the capture delay, authorizations there will lapse before capture and fail with E4021.

If the fraud rules exist, they most likely live outside this repo: in the payment provider's risk settings, in a separate fraud or risk service, or in a team runbook. Whoever owns payments or fraud operations should be able to give you the real numbers.
